steps: Wash the rosemary, tear the leaves off the stems and chop. In a bowl, whisk together the honey, lemon juice, lemon zest, rosemary, olive oil and salt. Put the chicken in a bag and pour in the marinade, rubbing it firmly into the meat. Close the bag and let it marinate for at least 1 hour, or preferably overnight.
Preheat the oven to 175°C. Place the chicken on a rack over a roasting pan and roast until the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, scrub the new potatoes and toss them in olive oil and salt. Add them to the roasting pan under the chicken so the juices drip over them, and roast until tender.
Rinse, spin and chop the parsley. Serve the chicken with the potatoes, sprinkled with chopped parsley and extra lemon zest.
Dice the chicken breast, sweet potato, onion and red pepper into roughly 1.5cm pieces.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the sweet potato for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it starts to soften and colour at the edges.
Add the onion and red pepper and cook for 3 minutes until softening.
Push the vegetables to one side, add the chicken and smoked paprika, and cook for 6-8 minutes, turning regularly, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink remaining.
Stir everything together, season with salt and pepper, and cook for a further 2 minutes until the sweet potato is tender when pierced with a knife.
Divide into 4 portions to serve now or store for later.
Marinate the chicken in tandoori paste for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge for deeper flavour.
Rinse the brown rice and cook in salted water according to the pack instructions, about 20-25 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Preheat a griddle pan or grill to high. Cook the marinated chicken for 6-7 minutes per side until charred at the edges and cooked through with no pink remaining.
Steam or stir-fry the mixed vegetables for 4-5 minutes until just tender.
Rest the chicken for a couple of minutes, then slice. Serve over the brown rice with the vegetables, a spoonful of plain yogurt and the strawberries on the side.
Cook the rice according to the pack instructions and set aside.
Heat a large pan over medium-high heat and brown the ground beef, breaking it up with a spoon, for 6-8 minutes until no pink remains; drain off any excess fat.
Add the frozen broccoli to the pan and cook for 5 minutes until heated through and tender.
Stir in the cooked rice and enchilada sauce, mixing well, and cook for a further 2-3 minutes until everything is warmed through and coated.
Season to taste, then portion out for the week and cool before refrigerating or freezing.
Peel and cube the potatoes, then boil in salted water for 15-18 minutes until a knife goes through easily (or cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the pack instructions).
Meanwhile, season the chicken breast and pan-fry in a little of the olive oil over medium heat for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through and no longer pink in the middle.
Steam or microwave the mixed vegetables for 4-5 minutes until just tender.
Drain the potatoes or pasta and toss with the remaining olive oil.
Slice the chicken and serve over the potatoes or pasta with the vegetables, finishing with grated parmesan if using.
Halve the new potatoes and boil in salted water for 15-18 minutes until tender when pierced with a knife, then drain.
Meanwhile, season the fish fillet and brush with a little olive oil. Grill or pan-fry for 3-4 minutes per side until it flakes easily with a fork.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a pan and wilt the spinach or chard for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until just tender.
Squeeze the lemon over the fish and serve with the potatoes and greens.
Cut the chicken into small chunks and fry them in oil in a pot for a few minutes.
Finely chop the chilli, pepper and garlic and put them into the pot when the chicken starts to brown. Sizzle for 1-2 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes and the apple juice and boil for 15 minutes.
In the meantime, cut the celeriac and the mango into 2cm cubes. Rapidly boil the celeriac for 1-2 minutes.
Stir the celeriac gently into the pot and season with salt and pepper.
Top with a dollop of crème fraîche and mango cubes, and serve with the rice.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Rinse the rice and cook in salted water according to the pack instructions, about 15 minutes, until tender.
Place the cod fillet on a lined baking tray, drizzle with olive oil, season, and top with a few lemon slices. Bake for 12-15 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Meanwhile, trim the green beans and steam or boil for 4-5 minutes until just tender.
Drain the rice, plate up with the beans and baked cod, and finish with a squeeze of the remaining lemon.
Peel and chop the potatoes and carrots into even chunks.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the potatoes and carrots together for 15-18 minutes until a knife goes through both easily.
Meanwhile, heat a lightly oiled frying pan over medium heat and cook the fish cakes for 4-5 minutes per side until golden and heated through.
Drain the potatoes and carrots and toss with the butter.
Serve the fish cakes with the buttered potatoes and carrots.
Rinse the rice and cook in salted water according to the pack instructions until tender, then drain.
Warm the cooked black beans gently in their broth over low heat for 5 minutes, mashing a few against the side of the pan to thicken the liquid slightly.
Season the chicken thigh and grill or pan-fry over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until browned and cooked through with no pink remaining.
Toast the farofa in a dry pan for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly golden and fragrant.
Toss sliced tomato and onion with a little oil, salt and pepper for the salad.
Plate the rice and beans together, top with the sliced grilled chicken, and serve with the farofa and tomato-onion salad.

For the stew, brown the beef stew meat in the oil with the chopped onion over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, then add the chopped tomato and a splash of water, cover and simmer for 45-60 minutes until the meat is tender.
For the sukuma wiki, shred the collard greens and sauté in a little oil with onion for 6-8 minutes until wilted and tender; season with salt.
For the ugali, bring water to the boil in a heavy pan, then gradually whisk in the maize flour to avoid lumps.
Reduce the heat and stir vigorously and continuously with a wooden spoon for 8-10 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan and forms a firm, smooth dough.
Turn the ugali out onto a plate or board and shape into a mound. Serve hot alongside the beef stew and sukuma wiki.
Dry roast the chickpea flour in a large skillet with the berbere powder, ground cardamom, cumin and garlic powder to make the shiro powder, then set aside.
Heat the oil and add the diced onion over low to medium heat for 1-2 minutes — don't let it brown.
Add the minced garlic along with the tomato paste and sauté for 30 seconds until the garlic is fragrant.
Add the shiro powder, along with salt and the water, and bring to a boil on medium heat.
Turn the heat down to low-medium and let it simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring at 5 minute increments so it doesn't stick.
Serve the shiro hot with the injera.
Rinse the rice and cook in salted water according to the pack instructions, about 15 minutes, until tender.
Season the salmon fillet and grill or pan-fry skin-side down for 4 minutes, then flip and cook for a further 2-3 minutes until it flakes easily.

Meanwhile, bring water to a gentle simmer for the miso soup and add a pinch of dried wakame to rehydrate, then remove from the heat and stir in the miso paste until dissolved — don't let it boil once the miso is added.
Add the cubed tofu to the soup and let it warm through for a minute.
Serve the salmon with the rice, miso soup and a small side of pickled vegetables.
Cook the rice in the water on the stovetop or using a rice cooker, then set aside to cool.
Wet both hands with water so the rice does not stick, then use your hands to form a portion of rice into a triangle.
Press an umeboshi into the centre and cover with another portion of rice, shaping into one triangle so the umeboshi is completely covered.
Fold a nori sheet in half and tear it apart. Using half a sheet, wrap the rice triangle in nori, making sure to completely cover the rice, then repeat to make a second onigiri.
For the miso soup, bring the kombu dashi to a gentle simmer, then remove from the heat and stir in the miso paste until dissolved — don't let it boil once the miso is in.
Add the cubed tofu and a pinch of wakame to the soup, warm through for a minute, and serve alongside the onigiri with the pickled vegetables.
